inventory_scope: Compiler-generated ALU/MAU spelling candidates plus separately scoped source-derived records; not an authoritative complete ISA or legality model.

findings: Every observed accepted `j` instruction output is a binary 426-bit word and every `m` instruction output is a binary 82-bit word. Accepted debug/DRAM records use `d`/`r` formats and are tracked separately because the default judge strips them from the scored instruction stream. These probes do not prove the output format for every accepted source line.
nop/0 is accepted and emits zero instruction words; nop/0 with a wait is rejected, so the zero-count no-wait form can be erased during normalization.
wait i00 is rejected; i01 and iFF are accepted; i100 is rejected.
Every u8 OMR destination selector was probed: exactly $omr1..$omr15 are accepted; $omr0 and $omr16..$omr255 are rejected.

Every u8 mask-read selector was probed: $imr0..$imr31 are accepted and $imr32..$imr255 are rejected. Every u8 selector was also probed for maskn, maskln, and masklln directives; each accepts 0..31 and rejects 32..255. This conflicts with the Rust MaskSource comment claiming entries 1 through 15.

Representative unknown `$qraw` operands in ALU source/destination, zero destination, matrix-read source, and L1BM source positions produce no assembler output; assemble3 aborts with return code -6 on these malformed tokens. This is sampled rejection evidence, not a proof over every Raw string.

SDM 3.6.4 requires simultaneous mask applications to use the same width; Section 3.6.2.1 also requires matching variable entry addresses. The same-width pair is accepted, while mixed widths, mixed entries, and a write-mask/zero-flush entry mismatch are rejected.

Mask-flag reads and OMR writes use distinct issue ports: a masked lpassa can issue with gmfma writing either the same or a different OMR entry. Multiple variable mask reads still require one shared entry, as shown by the accepted and rejected mask-application pair probes.

SDM 3.6.4 treats mask registers as PE operands and disallows multiple writes to that operand in one step. Two otherwise accepted operations that write OMR are rejected together, both for the same entry and for different entries.

After seeding the turnaround buffer with a valid PE-to-L1BM transfer, an ordinary L1BM source and the turnaround source $lbi are each accepted alone. Issuing both to PE destinations together is rejected with an l1bm_emit conflict, an implicit $lbf write conflict across the distinct L1BM issue groups.

The June 2026 manual's Section 3.6.4 describes an l2bmdars exception for simultaneous issue with another L2BM operation, but the bundled assemble3 rejects the focused l2bmdars+l2bmb line. The local encoder/model agreement is unresolved against the newer manual.

The l2bmdars companion matrix also rejected eight L2BM operation classes at each selector .0 and .1. This broadens the bundled assembler evidence but does not identify the newer manual's special exception or prove it cannot occur.
Matrix rows 0 through 15 are accepted; row 16 is rejected.

PE destination lists are not sized by source arity: lpassa accepts three outputs across LM1/GRF0/GRF1, and zero accepts LM0/LM1/GRF0/GRF1 plus OMR. The sampled duplicate-bank and nowrite combinations are rejected; this is not an exhaustive output grammar proof.
The issue checker now mirrors the sampled assembler rule that destination banks cannot repeat within one expression and `$nowrite` must be the sole destination.
Every u8 argument was probed for hbfe and hbfn; both accept exactly /6 through /9.
LM0/LM1 and GRF0/GRF1 accept aligned final addresses at widths 1, 2, and 4; their single-word capacities are respectively 4096 and 512, and the capacity address is rejected.
Each of the four explicit LM0 cycle addresses accepts 4095 and rejects 4096; madpe values 0 through 3 are accepted and 4 is rejected.

All 64 L1B set address/immode pairs in 0..7 are accepted, and address 8 and immode 8 are rejected; `l2bm@<l1b>` accepts 0..7 and rejects 8. Base-address register writes accept widths 1 and 2 but reject width 4.

For every documented MV grammar in Sections 3.5.8.2–3.5.8.25, generated zero-address probes accept sizes 64 and 32704 and reject 32768. The simple operand combinations are sampled evidence, not a proof of all accepted operands. The separate mvp probes show size zero is accepted, size one is rejected, and the size-field overflow at 32768 is rejected.

L1BM width-2 addresses require 4-word alignment and width-4 addresses require 8-word alignment, within the 8192-long-word capacity. The L2BM transfer source accepts 16-aligned addresses through 32752 and rejects 32760 (alignment) and 32768 (range).
Wait tags 1 through 255 are accepted; 0 and 256 are rejected.
Matrix rows 0..15 were checked using gmread. The tested matrix operand widths are instruction-specific: gmread/gmwrite accept width 2 and reject width 4, while gmmul accepts widths 2 and 4.

$lb8188 is accepted while $lb8192 fails the 13-bit encoding field; the L1BM address must also be 4-word aligned. Every l1bmm@ and l1bmm4@ selector 0..15 is accepted, and @16 is rejected for both forms.
DAR address 1023 is accepted and 1024 is rejected; `$lc...@.<l2b>` accepts selectors 0 and 1 and rejects 2.

For l1bmd, each explicit signed offset from -255 through +255 was accepted in both operand directions (PE-to-L1BM gather and L1BM-to-PE distribution); -256 and +256 were rejected in both directions. The manual documents useful offsets 0..15. The Rust visualizer parser now stores the value in i16 and enforces this experimentally established assembler range; its boundary regression is separate from this assembler-only probe. Neither check proves global parser completeness.

The assembler accepts d set, d get and r input records, but the challenge judge's default solution sanitizer retains only j/m instruction rows; these records are filtered before execution. The scored program therefore excludes debug and DRAM initialization records.

A zero instruction with one destination in each of LM0, LM1, GRF0, GRF1, T and OMR is accepted; duplicate destinations within each of those six categories are rejected. This bounds observed destination categories for these probes, but Rust's VSM parser itself still stores all tokens after the fixed source prefix as destinations, and the assembler probes are not a universal parser-to-encoding theorem.

Same-expression destination checks reject duplicate output classes even when the operand values differ (LM0 at two addresses, two OMR entries), reject repeated nowrite, and reject multiple matrix-write destinations. A single nowrite destination is accepted. These checks support finite destination arity for the sampled opcodes but do not establish a bound for every opcode spelling.
Judge flags can preserve d get/d set, but the normal challenge invocation does not set them; the d-set invalidation applies only when such a record is retained.

Selected valid-operand combinations of l2bmdars with l2bmb, l2bmb2, l2bmd, l2bm@, l2bmr*, l2bmr2* and l2bmi were rejected. This does not cover the manual's unspecified special l2bmdars issue condition.

The assembler accepts `nop; wait i01` and rejects nop with an ALU expression; the zero-count nop/wait pair is also rejected. MV and PE expressions cannot be combined on one source line in either order in the tested forms.
selected_parser_boundary_experiment.scope: Only listed probes. Acceptance/encoding evidence is not proof of complete ISA ranges or semantics.

encoded_word_universe.scope: Selected bounded candidate universe: all bit patterns in fixed-width PE/MV words. It over-approximates accepted source output; source-to-word correspondence and step semantics remain open.

phase_2_resolution.legal_policy: Successful source normalization defines the candidate domain; operational issue/hazard/disabled-unit errors are step failures.

hazard_aware_transition.implemented: PE and block hazard event extraction, violation-to-failure behavior, bounded event history, and deterministic completion of same-tag pending MV transfers before a wait line
hazard_aware_transition.stalled_issue_guard: Both scheduled and deterministic hazard-aware runners reject new issues while a PE wait is stalled
hazard_aware_transition.pe_memory_address_modifiers: Negated/extended/rounded value modifiers are erased only for hazard address resolution; bank, region, t-indirect/madpe fields, and destination write mask are retained
hazard_aware_transition.malformed_address_mode_handling: Unsupported direct PE-memory widths and t-indirect/madpe bank combinations fail before hazard lowering

hazard_address_resolution.scope: A NormalizedLine that passes parsedNormalizedLinePEAddressModesValid has total PE hazard-event extraction across each operand, each expression, every PE, and all four cycles.
hazard_address_resolution.remaining: Prove source parser/normalizer correspondence establishes the address-mode guard for every accepted source line; block-hazard extraction totality and hazard runtime conformance remain separate.

hazard_aware_transition.disabled_forwarding: Producer absence is represented as poison with validity=false and consumed forward operands fail; unresolved ALU/MAU/mread output remains unknown with validity=true; noforward preserves payload and validity state; L1-to-PE validity has its separate retained-state rule
hazard_aware_transition.l1_to_pe_absent_behavior: Rust machine.rs retains prior LBF payload and error when the step has no L1-to-PE producer; Lean reference transition preserves the same per-cycle slot
hazard_aware_transition.scope_limit: Source-parser correspondence for PE address modes remains unproved; five forwarding experiment programs remain assembler-rejected and lack whole-program conformance evidence

mask_directive_state_connection.condition: No PE issue is already stalled for the public deterministic runner.
mask_directive_state_connection.effect: Only machine maskDirective changes; PE/block histories, stalled marker, and hazardClock are preserved.

positive_nop_state_connection.scope: Positive nop count with no wait.
positive_nop_state_connection.effect: Advances the hazard clock by issue cost, emits no hazard events, and prunes PE/block history against the four-word retention window.

wait_nop_completion_connection.scope: A positive nop with a valid wait tag, scheduled after an incomplete tag and then resumed after completion of the final operation with that tag.
wait_nop_completion_connection.effect: The scheduled run enters the stalled state, completes the named MV, resumes the nop, advances hazardClock by its count, emits no hazard events, prunes PE/block history, and clears the stalled marker.
wait_nop_completion_connection.remaining: General PE wait-line effects and Rust conformance remain open.
wait_nop_completion_connection.two_completion_scope: Two individually scheduled completions with the same tag; after the first, the tag remains incomplete and the PE stays stalled; after the second, the tag is complete and the nop resumes.
wait_nop_completion_connection.drain_scope: If the tag is initially incomplete and completePendingMvTagAll succeeds, the result marks the tag complete, contains no pending entry with that tag, and preserves all untagged or differently tagged entries in original order. The deterministic runner then executes the wait nop with the integrated clock/history transition, for any finite queue length within the fuel bound.

remaining: Prove PE/block hazard extraction total for every accepted source form and prove noforward/disabled-producer lifecycle against the reference executor for all forwarding units.
Prove universal source-parser/assembler correspondence into fixed-width encoded words.
Connect encoded words to transition semantics and seal MNCore.machine.

phase_3_state_footprint.coverage: All executable normalized line constructors and all parsed PE opcodes, plus MV and nop rows.

partial_pe_step.scope: one PE, four integer-register cycles; MV, forwarding, and hazards remain unknown

phase_3_state_footprint.limitation: Footprints are syntactic read/write candidates. Normalized executable lines align with InstructionLine footprints, and the mask-directive hazard-aware transition is connected exactly; general successful integrated instruction transitions still lack a footprint frame theorem.

mask_directive.footprint: normalizedLineFootprint marks maskControl and omits hazardClock
mask_directive.proved_effect: Updates only State.maskDirective within the machine; preserves PE history, block history, stalled-issue marker, and machine hazard clock. The public deterministic runner requires no pre-existing stalled PE issue.

positive_nop_without_wait.scope: All positive nop counts with no wait, using the integrated hazard-aware transition.
positive_nop_without_wait.proved_effect: Advances machine hazardClock by count, generates no PE/block events, preserves the stalled marker, and filters prior histories by whether each event remains within four issue words of the new clock. The public runner requires no current stall.

completed_wait_nop.effect: After the tag is complete, the positive wait nop advances the clock, emits no events, prunes old histories, and releases the stalled issue.

completed_wait_nop_two_transfers.effect: A positive wait nop remains stalled through the first same-tag completion while the tag is incomplete; the second completion releases the nop, advances the clock by count, emits no hazard events, and prunes histories.

wait_nop_arbitrary_tag_drain.scope: When the tag starts incomplete, any successful finite completePendingMvTagAll run leaves no pending operation carrying that tag.
wait_nop_arbitrary_tag_drain.effect: After such a successful drain, the deterministic runner executes the wait nop, advances clock, and prunes hazard histories.

The candidates omit L1BM/L2BM transfer opcodes, wait/noforward, and any manual spelling absent from the compiler inventory.

limitations: Only one compiler-generated operand template per syntax candidate is used.

finite_carrier_proofs.scope: Finite carrier for structured PE operands under numeric envelopes. commit_order_frame.rust_source_order: Rust computes all producers from pre-issue operands, applies matrix-register writes, then commits PE destinations.
commit_order_frame.lean_order: The Lean whole-state line transition commits PE producer destinations, applies MAU PE destinations, then commits matrix-register writes.
commit_order_frame.scope: When the MAU producer and following matrix-write stage succeed, the combined transition preserves the PE registers, forwarding payloads and validity, and PE context produced by the MAU stage. The matrix-write-only frame theorem also covers the same fields for PE producer destinations. This establishes the corresponding state-field noninterference for the represented commit order.
commit_order_frame.issue_source: viz/core/src/issue.rs:check rejects duplicate PE memory-bank writers and multiple mask-register writers in one issue line.

mau_commit_frame.scope: For every successful matrix-MAU producer, including PE output commit across all MABs and global poison propagation, matrix registers equal their pre-issue values. The isolated PE commit helper also preserves L1BM and turnaround state, block memory, DAR/DARBUF, MV tags and queue, mask directive, and hazard clock.

known_failure_classification.behavior: A matrix-MAU calculation with a missing, non-matrix, or row-selected first source, or a missing required vector/accumulator source, returns failure instead of unknown.
known_failure_classification.rust_reference: viz/core/src/machine.rs::Machine::compute_mat explicitly rejects a non-matrix first source; viz/core/src/vsm.rs::parse_expr rejects too few operands before Machine::step.
known_failure_classification.scope: For direct Lean AST inputs, malformed missing sources are classified as failure; parser-produced instructions reject insufficient source counts before execution. This does not establish complete Rust/Lean command conformance for valid matrix-MAU instructions.

source_unknown_classification.scope: For one participating PE, when parsedFloatMAUSourceAttrs? successfully lowers the operand to a direct-memory or forwarding input, the MAU source reader cannot return .unknown if every valid forwarding slot in the state is resolved. Disabled forwarding and invalid lane decoding remain known failures.
source_unknown_classification.mab_scope: When the same successful memory/forwarding source-lowering condition holds for each of the four participating PEs, the source-ordered MAB reader cannot return .unknown. Its recursive proof runner is proved equal to the original loop-based accumulation, including failure/unknown short-circuiting and lane order.
source_unknown_classification.connection_limit: Connect MAB output through destination writes/MAUF commit and full issue-line transition; derive all calculation/source premises from parser-produced instructions and legal forwarding state.
source_unknown_classification.lowering_miss_behavior: A memory/forward source that cannot be lowered is a known execution failure, matching Rust compute_mat read_raw_elems errors; .unknown is reserved for unresolved forwarding state.
source_unknown_classification.calculation_scope: For each matrix-MAU kind and its parser-arity source list, if the MAB vector read is known and (for fma) the accumulator read is known, the calculation executor cannot return .unknown. The fma accumulator format is explicitly double for D and single otherwise.
source_unknown_classification.calculation_output_scope: Given a known matrix-MAU calculation result and a matrix-MAU opcode, PE output packing over all four PEs returns only failure or success. Packing preserves per-PE bus/flag placement through the same ordered PE traversal.

source_algorithm_audit.remaining: Run command-level Rust differentials for source operands, matrix layout, row masks, PE packing, flags, poison, and forwarding; the arithmetic-only comparison does not establish compute_mat or whole-machine conformance.
source_algorithm_audit.source_mask_lowering: parsedFloatMAUSourceAttrs? accepts masked and unmasked memory operands, then lowers the same mask-free memory input. Rust read_raw_untraced ignores the operand mask during reads.

destination_lowering_miss_classification.scope_limit: This classifies known lowering failures; proving the full PE write loop and whole-line matrix-MAU transition unknown-free still requires premises for calculation outputs and legal destination forms.

destination_write_knownness.scope: For each kind, successful memory/forward lowering across all four MAB cycles plus forwardingSourceResolved implies the complete ordered four-cycle/four-PE destination write executor cannot return .unknown. fma requires both vector and accumulator lowering at every cycle.
destination_write_knownness.remaining: For lines that co-issue matrix writes, establish matrix-write lowering/read knownness and issue constraints; then derive parser/source premises for matrix-MAU producers and connect the full instruction-line transition.
destination_write_knownness.mab_sequence_scope: A sequence of MAB transitions is unknown-free when each transition is unknown-free for every intermediate committed state; the state-dependent premise explicitly follows the state threaded through the sequence.
destination_write_knownness.all_mab_sequence_scope: For any coordinate list, if each coordinate and every cycle has successful vector lowering (and fma accumulator lowering) under one resolved readState, the entire state-threaded MAB sequence cannot return .unknown. Read lowering is based on readState while commit state is threaded separately.
destination_write_knownness.producer_filter_behavior: executeParsedMatrixMAUProducer classifies multiple selected matrix-MAU producers as failure, matching issue.rs one-expression-per-mau-calc-group rejection.
destination_write_knownness.producer_scope: Given a producer filter containing exactly the shaped MAU expression, successful source lowering on all participating MABs/cycles and resolved forwarding imply the producer stage cannot return .unknown. Poison propagation after successful MAB execution is included.
destination_write_knownness.mau_and_matrix_write_scope: The MAU producer/write stage composes without unknown when the producer is known. If the issue line has no matrix-register write producer, the subsequent matrix-write stage is known by its empty-filter branch, so the full executeParsedMatrixMAUAndWrites composition is known.

matrix_write_lowering_miss.behavior: Any matrix-write lowering miss is a known failure, including mem/forward source forms whose address/source fields cannot be represented.

matrix_write_forward_validation.behavior: With forwardingSourceResolved, each PE bus read and the four-PE bus aggregation cannot return .unknown. Disabled forwarding and poison reads fail; known memory/fixed/forwarding values pass through a bus preparation function proved unknown-free. The matrix-write cycle, arbitrary cycle-list executor, and four-cycle executor also cannot return .unknown for a matrix-write expression under the same forwarding premise. Filtered multiple matrix writes compose at one MAB, across any coordinate list, and with a known MAU producer into the matrix-MAU-plus-write stage.
matrix_write_forward_validation.scope_limit: The premise excludes enabled forwarding slots whose payload remains unknown; the MAU producer must separately be known. This proves the matrix-MAU-and-write substage, while earlier and later whole-line stages and other instruction families remain outstanding.

source_algorithm_audit.mau_and_matrix_write_scope: The MAU producer/write stage composes without unknown when the producer is known and forwarding sources are resolved, including nonempty matrix-write producer lists. The empty-filter theorem remains a weaker special case.

whole_line_no_unknown_composition.behavior: For a top-level accepted PE instruction line with supported producers, no unsupported Rust ALU, and completed waits, the ordered whole-line transition cannot return .unknown when each selected producer stage is itself known for every possible preceding state. The shared-block stage condition is derived directly from forwardingSourceResolved using the existing per-expression and source-order composition proofs. The 4096-PE prefix is itself composed from a per-PE unknown-free premise using source-order induction. The float-ReLU issue stage is reduced from a whole-stage condition to a per-selected-expression, per-PE, per-intermediate-state condition and composed over 4096 PEs. The MSL/MSR stage is now reduced to per-selected-expression/per-PE/per-intermediate-state conditions and composed across its 4096-PE traversal. The block-float stage is reduced to per-selected-expression/per-MAB/per-intermediate-state conditions and composed over the complete MAB coordinate list. The matrix-MAU/write command stage now derives its matrix-write/MAB traversal premise from resolved forwarding and retains only matrix-MAU producer knownness as an explicit stage condition. The matrix-MAU producer premise is further reduced to each selected expression’s transition at each MAB and every intermediate state; the MAB traversal and producer filter are composed using existing generic theorems. The matrix-MAU MAB condition now sits at the cycle calculation boundary; the destination/forwarding write loop and the MAB state commit are discharged by composition. The remaining matrix-MAU cycle-calculation premise is characterized by one of mul/add/passa/fma, a recognized precision format, and lowered vector sources (plus the accumulator source for fma); resolved forwarding then proves the calculation known. The per-PE forwarding update is independently proved unknown-free because it only supplies supported issue summaries to the reference update function.
whole_line_no_unknown_composition.scope_limit: The matrix-MAU calculation condition is an explicit format/source-lowering predicate per selected expression/MAB/cycle plus resolved forwarding. A matrix-read expression four-cycle transition is known when operand lowering resolves at each cycle. Integer ALU four-cycle execution is known from per-cycle lowering and the condition that every forwarding slot for each cycle is non-unknown; source-specific read-known premises are derivable from that condition. For zero/immediate producers, the public destination lowerer proves every memory target has known source reads, and every ParsedMask flush selector resolves for all register states because selectors are total over pattern bits and Fin 256 entries. The mixed integer-ALU/constant/matrix-read line cycle runner now composes per-expression unknown-freedom over arbitrary expression lists, including state-threaded output slots. A single readiness predicate selects the per-cycle lowering and forwarding-slot obligations by operation and discharges the full mixed line transition. The integer-ALU branch condition is now derived from per-cycle lowerer success and forwardingSourceResolved on the whole-machine state (which supplies non-unknown stateForwardingSlots); deriving lowerer success from accepted source lines and resolved state remains open; constant expressions now use per-cycle destination lowering, and matrix-read expressions use per-cycle source/destination lowering plus total flush selection, as do float-MAU cycles, full Rust/Lean equivalence, and other line forms.

completion_scheduling.scope: Completes any pending issue, including an untagged MV, by its current pending-queue index; commits the captured writes and marks a tag complete only when no pending issue with that tag remains.
completion_scheduling.tagged_wait_release: A matching tag releases the stalled PE wait only after the last pending issue with that tag completes; untagged and unrelated completions leave it stalled.

Whether duplicate live tags are legal on hardware remains unresolved; the model conservatively waits for all pending operations carrying the tag.

obligations.untagged_mv_progress: Represented by ScheduledEvent.completeMvIssue; wait release requires the matching tag to have no remaining pending operations. Duplicate live-tag legality on hardware remains unresolved.
